analysis.title: 2026 Deloitte Holiday Retail Survey: Balancing budgets and keeping spirits bright
key_insights: Average expected household holiday spend is $1,654, up 4% YoY, and 79% of respondents expect higher prices on holiday items (77% in 2025, 69% in 2024).
Spending on retail goods is expected to rise 10% YoY to $988, while holiday activities (travel, events, hosting) fall 4% YoY to $666.
Gen Z and millennials are expected to make up 50% of holiday spending for the first time in the survey, and both groups plan double-digit YoY spending increases.
Income gap: households earning $200K+ plan to spend $3,607 on average, more than 5x the $693 expected by those earning under $50K.

38% of shoppers are 'holiday value seekers' (five or more money-saving behaviors) yet plan to spend 12% more than other shoppers. 62% bought private label in the past six months vs 46% of others, and 35% shop off-price vs 21%.

Shopping is starting earlier: 22% plan to start sooner than last year, 28% of budgets will be spent by end of October (highest in six years, vs 24% in 2025), and 1 in 4 already bought holiday items in June promotions.

October sales events are gaining participation: 42% plan to join, up 18 pp over three years (24% in 2023, 38% in 2024, 40% in 2025). Thanksgiving week remains the main event, with shopper activity at 77% in late November and 78% in early December.

54% of shoppers plan to spend most of their budget at e-commerce or mass merchants. Online is 55% of planned retail holiday budgets ($548) vs in-store 45% ($440), and in-store spend is planned up 12% YoY.

50% of shoppers plan to gift an experience (47% in 2025, 39% in 2024), and 79% of experience gifters want to pair it with a physical item, which creates cross-merchandising opportunities for retailers.

Gen AI is the primary tool for at least one holiday shopping task for 39% of respondents, but only 16% would let it complete a purchase with permission, and 66% worry about how gen AI assistants use their data.
Planned spend rises with digital tool use: shoppers using all three tech tools (search, social, gen AI) plan $2,893 vs $1,175 for non-tech users.

Luxury interest is rising: 49% will consider luxury gifts (44% in 2025), and 49% say luxury is a worthy investment (39% in 2025). Gen Z luxury consideration is 72% (57% in 2025). Luxury gift shoppers plan to spend 56% more on gifts than others.
Self-gifting: 33% plan to self-gift, led by Gen Z (49%) and millennials (42%). Average self-gift spend is $299, up 13% YoY.
Gift categories: clothing and accessories is the most common (67% in 2026 vs 63% in 2025), and Gen Z gifting of clothing rises to 76% from 67%. 33% plan to gift cash vs 29% in 2025.
Survey fielded Aug 26 to Sept 10, 2026 with 4,000 US consumers and a margin of error of plus or minus 2 percentage points.

sector_views.rationale: Budgets are rising 4% YoY, but spend is shifting toward retail goods and away from activities. Value-seeking is widespread, and spend is consolidating at online and mass merchants.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Survey-based expected spend. Retail goods are expected up 10% to $988 and activities down 4% to $666.
Consumers expect higher prices, which supports nominal spend growth and the value-seeking behavior.

macro_indicators.reading: 45% expect the economy to stay the same or improve (43% in 2025)

risk_factors: 79% of consumers expect higher prices, and shoppers are hunting for value (38% are value seekers), which may pressure retailer margins and promotions.
Holiday activities and travel/events spend is down 4% YoY, and spending is highly concentrated by income and generation.
Only 16% would let gen AI complete a purchase and 66% worry about data use, which limits agentic commerce adoption near term.
Earlier shopping and promotions (June, October events) may pull demand forward from the Thanksgiving-week peak.
charts_described: Average expected holiday spend by year: $1,778 in 2024, $1,595 in 2025, $1,654 in 2026, split into retail goods and holiday activities.

Gift categories chart: clothing and accessories 67% in 2026 vs 63% in 2025, toys and hobbies 61% in both years, food and beverage 55% vs 54%, gift cards 54% in both years.
